originality.rationale: Pilla (arXiv:2606.25885v1) provides the homogeneous operator and basic boundedness/compactness, not exact S2 coefficient norms. Bellavita–Dellepiane–Stylogiannis (arXiv:2606.15875v1) treats one-variable weighted Hardy and factorable matrices, not the multivariate row-multiplicity formula. Searches of published mathematical records and accessible overlap records found no equivalent two-dimensional logarithmic anomaly or all-dimensional exact coefficient series. The classical d=1 case is explicitly excluded from the novelty assertion. Best-knowledge rather than exhaustive priority. Bellavita–Dellepiane–Stylogiannis (arXiv:2503.21930v1) Theorems 1.3 and 5.8 were additionally inspected in open-access full text: their one-variable Schatten characterization does not assert the new multivariable row law.
residual_risks: Older work on weighted factorable matrices could imply the exact identity after a nontrivial decomposition; no exhaustive priority certification.

value.rationale: The natural multivariable Rhaly tuple has an exact and complete S2 coefficient norm in every fixed ambient dimension. A genuine \(d=2\) harmonic multiplicity produces an exceptional squared-log critical divergence and a distinct logarithmic power-weight threshold; dimensions 1 and at least 3 have single-log divergence. This motivated, complete ideal invariant is neither an arbitrary numerical slice nor mere restatement of one-variable prior work.
